Apple has once again stepped up, contributing to relief efforts in response to a deadly natural disaster. Here are the details.

Apple Pledges Support for Recovery Work After Deadly Floods in Nepal

Apple CEO Tim Cook said tonight that the company will donate to support rescue and recovery efforts, helping those affected by flash floods and mudslides in Nepal and Tibet. The disaster has already claimed hundreds of lives.

The disaster began on Wednesday, when a section of glacier in the Himalayas collapsed downstream. The debris temporarily blocked a river, which later burst, sending a torrent of floodwater and mud downstream, killing hundreds and leaving many more homeless. Villages, roads, bridges and other infrastructure have also been severely damaged.

Just days before Cook made this commitment, Apple had announced donations to support relief efforts following an earthquake in Indonesia. In recent months, the company has also lent a hand to emergency relief in Venezuela, Southern Europe, Japan and elsewhere.

In addition to actively responding to natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also runs an internal "Employee Giving" programme, which has raised more than US$880 million to date through a donation matching mechanism.
